teaching_blocks.title: The situation
teaching_blocks.content: A webhook signature authenticates the delivered bytes. Parsing and rewriting a body before verification can lose the exact input the publisher signed.

teaching_blocks.title: The rule and its boundary
teaching_blocks.content: Read await request.body() to obtain the raw request bytes for signature verification before parsing or modifying the webhook body.

teaching_blocks.title: How to use the rule
teaching_blocks.content: Verify every delivery with the publisher's supported SDK or verification library against the raw bytes and endpoint signing secret, following that publisher's signing format rather than inventing a canonicalization. Reject missing or invalid signatures before processing the event, and do not disclose the verification secret or failure's internal details in the response. Test a valid signed delivery and deliveries with a modified body or absent signature, checking that only the valid delivery reaches event processing.

teaching_blocks.title: Reason through an example
teaching_blocks.content: Read raw bytes with await request.body() and verify every delivery through the publisher-supported SDK or library using the endpoint signing secret and supplied signing format. Only then move to parsing and processing. Test a valid signed body, a modified body and an absent signature. Only the valid delivery should reach event processing, and rejection should not reveal the secret or verification internals.

teaching_blocks.title: Keep this distinction
teaching_blocks.content: Do not invent your own canonicalized body format. Verify the raw bytes using the publisher's supported signing contract.

visual_anchor.purpose: Make the handler's order visible: raw-byte acquisition, signature presence check, provider-supported verification with the endpoint secret, safe rejection, and processing only after verification. Place the three test outcomes beside the corresponding branches.

practice_anchor.objective: Implement one provider's webhook authenticity check using await request.body(), the supplied signature header, the endpoint signing secret, and the provider-supported verification library.
practice_anchor.success: A valid signed delivery reaches event processing. The same delivery with modified body bytes, and a delivery without a signature, are rejected before processing with responses that expose neither the secret nor verification internals.

live_code.required_skill: Verify the original request bytes before parsing or processing, using the provider's supported signing contract, and test the acceptance and rejection paths.

live_code.starter_state_intent: Provide an async webhook handler, validated endpoint signing-secret configuration, one provider's installed verification library and documented signature header, a supplied event-processing recorder, and a valid signed raw-body fixture. Leave the verification gate and the three delivery tests incomplete.
live_code.observable_success: Tests submit the valid fixture unchanged, submit modified bytes with its original signature, and omit the signature. Only the unchanged signed delivery invokes the processing recorder; both rejected deliveries return generic failures without sensitive details.
